title: Dan Wake
author: Florence Madu
desc: Bean flour, cassava flour and baobab powder bound with beef stock into a sticky dough, moulded by fingertip and boiled fifteen to twenty minutes.
longDesc: Dan wake means son of beans and it is the north's dumpling. Two small party cups of bean flour, one of cassava flour, two teaspoons of baking soda or potash and two tablespoons of kuka powder are mixed dry, and then beef stock is added bit by bit until the mixture becomes a soft sticky dough. Rough shapes are moulded with the fingertips and dropped into boiling water, stirred at the ten-minute mark, and done in fifteen to twenty minutes. The interesting thing is the kuka — here it is a binder rather than a soup thickener.
ingredients: 2 tsp baking soda, or 2 tsp edible potash
Beef stock — see the note on the missing quantity
steps: Mix all the dry ingredients in a bowl: bean flour, cassava flour, baking soda and kuka powder.
If you are using edible potash instead of baking soda, mix it with a small quantity of water, sieve it, and add only the liquid.
Start adding the beef stock bit by bit, mixing as you go, till you get a soft sticky dough.
Boil water in a pot with adequate space for the dumplings.
Mould the dough using your fingertips into rough shapes and drop them into the boiling water.
Cover the pot and continue cooking on medium heat.
After 10 minutes, stir and continue cooking. It should be done in 15 to 20 minutes on low to medium heat.
chefTips: Add the stock bit by bit. Soft and sticky is the target and you cannot take liquid back out.
Sieve the potash and use only the liquid, leaving the sediment. Same rule as every other alkali step in this collection.
Mould with the fingertips and do not aim for neat. Rough shapes are correct and they hold together better than rolled balls.
Do not stir for the first ten minutes. The dumplings need to set before anything touches them.
Plenty of space in the pot. Crowded dumplings stick together into one mass.
Kuka powder here is a binder, not a thickener. Same ingredient as miyan kuka (NGA087), completely different structural role.
The beef stock is the hydrating liquid and it carries no quantity on the source page. Expect to need somewhere around a cup to a cup and a half for this quantity of flour, added gradually.
commonMistakes: Adding all the stock at once.
Rolling smooth balls, which cook unevenly.
sources: Adapted from 'Nigerian Dan Wake', All Nigerian Recipes — no author specified on the page, credited to the site. Local name as printed: Dan Wake, 'literally "Son of Beans"'. Headnote as printed: 'Dan Wake which literally means Son of Beans is a Northern Nigerian recipe. You can call Dan Wake Beans Dumplings in English because the preparation is similar.' YIELD AS PRINTED: Serves 3 people.
Quantities exactly as printed: 2 small party cups beans flour; 1 small party cup cassava flour; 2 teaspoons baking soda or 2 teaspoons edible potash; 2 tablespoons kuka powder; Beef stock.

TWO NOTES ON THOSE QUANTITIES. First, 'Beef stock' carries NO QUANTITY — and it is the hydrating liquid, which makes it the load-bearing omission. The estimate in the tips is labelled as an estimate. Second, 'small party cups' is a non-standard unit and it has not been converted.

Method as printed: mix all the dry ingredients; if using edible potash, mix with a small quantity of water, sieve, and add the liquid only; 'Start adding the beef stock bit by bit and mix the Dan Wake ingredients at the same time till you get a soft sticky dough'; set aside; boil water in a pot with adequate space for the dumplings; mould using fingertips into rough shapes and drop into the boiling water; cover and continue on medium heat; 'After 10 minutes, stir and continue cooking.'
DONENESS CUE as printed: 'It should be done in 15 to 20 minutes on low to medium heat.'

AN INTERESTING STRUCTURAL POINT: kuka (baobab) powder appears here as a BINDER IN A DUMPLING, not as a soup thickener. Same ingredient as in miyan kuka (NGA087), different structural role — which is worth noticing because it tells you something about what baobab powder actually does.

Edible potash is listed as interchangeable with baking soda at the same quantity, 2 teaspoons. They are chemically different bases of different strength and no source consulted quantifies the substitution — see NGA120 and the note at NGA056 on the four interchangeable alkalis.

LEADS NOT RETRIEVED: Afrolems has a danwake and a 'Glazed Danwake' — the latter self-evidently a modern invention by its title — and Dobby's Signature has 'Danwake (Bean flour Dumplings)'. None was fetched.
healthBenefits: Bean flour is high in plant protein, folate and soluble fibre.
Baobab powder is high in vitamin C and calcium.
culturalNote: Dan wake is cheap, filling northern street food, sold from a basin with palm oil, pepper and kuli kuli crumbled over the top. Son of beans is a fair name for it — it is what bean flour becomes when you want something to chew rather than something to swallow, and the baobab powder in the dough is a distinctly northern touch that no southern dumpling has.
